raw_case_text:
A 62-year-old man with signs of progression of the underlying disease (chronic lymphocytic leukaemia, CLL) was admitted to the Department of Haemato-oncology and Bone Marrow Transplantation in Poland in February 2010. According to the patient's medical history, the neoplasm was diagnosed in 2006 in Rotterdam, the Netherlands. Until 2010, the patient was treated with chlorambucil in a foreign clinic. Necessary tests were performed, including the determination of the immunophenotype. Laboratory tests showed a slightly increased WBC level (11.87 K/microl), LUC level (0.6 K/microl) and number of lymphocytes (LYM) (5.36 K/microl) (45.1% CD5+23+19+ B-cells), while the LDH level (280 IU/l) and beta2M level (1.88 mg/l) were in the normal range, with a normal count of red blood cells and platelets. The diagnosis of CLL according to Rai's stage 2 was maintained in accordance with the initial diagnosis and the FC cytostatic system (cyclophosphamide + fludarabine) was used in ambulatory treatment. From March 2013, the patient was treated with human normal immunoglobulins in subcutaneous administration due to the reduced levels of IgM (4.85 g/l), IgM (0.14 g/l), and IgA (0.34 g/l). In 2015, the patient was urgently admitted to the ward with suspicion of disease progression - weakness, sweating, peripheral lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly in the ultrasound (USG). Laboratory tests revealed massive leucocytosis (WBC - 68.5 K/microl). Virological tests for HCV and HBV were negative. Immunophenotype and cytogenetic tests were ordered. The flow cytometry of peripheral blood confirmed the domination of monoclonal B-cells - 80% lymphocytes with the presence of antigens: CD5+, CD19+, CD23+, CD20+, CD38+/-, CD200+. Genetic testing showed absence of characteristic mutations. Associated diseases: paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, type 2 diabetes, erosive gastritis (Helicobacter pylori positive), atherosclerosis, etc. The patient was qualified for immunochemotherapy in the BR scheme (rituximab + bendamustine), and from the second half of 2016, doxorubicin, vincristine, cyclophosphamide, prednisone in the CHOP scheme. Partial remission of the disease was achieved. However, in the second half of 2017, due to the increase in WBC to 131 K/microl, it was decided to administer rituximab and ibrutinib. The presence of anti-HBc total antibodies was detected and lamivudine was introduced prophylactically. The leukogram (Fig. 1) and peripheral blood immunophenotype results were presented by 43% of CD5+, CD19+, CD23+, CD20+, CD38+/-, CD200+, CD22+, CD43+, CD71-, sIgM-, sLambda-, sKappa+, ZAP-70+- B-cells (Fig. 2). Due to the diagnosed atelectatic-inflammatory changes in the middle and lower fields of the right lung in computed tomography (CT), the patient was referred for bronchoscopy, which was performed in 2017. After obtaining preliminary results of the bronchoscopy, Candida tropicalis was detected. It was decided to use a fluconazole antifungal treatment. The final histopathological diagnosis of mediastinal nodes collected during the bronchoscopy also revealed infiltrates corresponding to chronic lymphocytic leukaemia. In a 2018 ultrasound of the abdominal cavity, the liver was still expanded, with enlarged lymph nodes along the vessels and in the hilum of the liver (1.09 x 0.77 cm and 1.14 x 0.53 cm). The patient remained under constant care of the Haemato-oncology Clinic.
Due to the described inflammatory changes in the ultra- sound of the colon, a colonoscopy was recommended during the stay in the gastroenterology ward. In the collected specimen sent for histopathological examination, there was found, inter alia, an Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)- positive mucocutaneous ulcer with accompanying lesions of inflammatory bowel disease. In 2021, the patient stayed at the Department of Clinical Immunology due to deep hypogammaglobulinaemia (IgG - 1.83%) in the course of the underlying disease, in connection with recurrent infections requiring frequent antibiotic therapy. The performed tests revealed unregulated diabetes (glycated haemoglobin HbA1c - 10.9%), slight leucocytosis with lymphocytosis (WBC - 11.68 K/microl, LYM - 7.27 K/microl (62.2%)), microcytic anaemia (RBC - 5.06 G/microl, HGB - 10.7 g/dl, HCT - 35.8%, MCV - 70.8 fl), transferrin and iron deficiency (Tf - 1.5 g/l [N: 2.0-3.6], Fe - 7.4 microg/ml [N: 50-212]), increased inflammatory parameters (calprotectin - 473.1 microg/g [N: < 120], CRP - 44.0 mg/l). Moreover, active CMV (CMV-DNA - 6.02 x 102 CMV copies/ml) and EBV (EBV-DNA - 3.12 x 104 DNA copies/ml) infection was found and valaciclovir was included in the treatment. Based on the viraemia result, sequential treatment of rituximab was started once a week. Control viral load testing after 2 doses of rituximab showed a reduction of viral load to 2.82 x 103 DNA copies/ml. A history of significant weight loss, weakness, low-grade fever and abdominal pain was revealed. The patient underwent specialist diagnostics again due to the suspicion of disease progression. Cells with the immunophenotype characteristic of CLL were excluded. An analysis of marker expression using the flow cytometry of peripheral blood showed the presence of approximately 48.2% natural killer cells (NK cells) with CD2+, CD7+, CD3-, CD16+, CD56+, CD8+/-, CD4-, Cyt3+/-, CD38+, CD43+, CD5-, CD19-, CD30-, CD34-, TdT- immunophenotype (Fig. 3). Bone marrow trepanobiopsy was performed, and imaging examinations were updated. The presence of about 10.1% NK cells with the immunophenotype as above was confirmed in the bone marrow, and in the myelogram lymphocytes that may correspond to the morphology of NK cells were observed (Fig. 4). The trepanobiopsy results confirmed the infiltration of small lymphoid cells (CD45+), which constitute about 20% of the bone marrow cells, about 1/3 of which are T-cells (CD3+, CD5+, CD8+, CD4-, CD20-, CD23-). There were no infiltrations characteristic of CLL. Due to the lack of access and the insufficient size of the lymph nodes, it was impossible to collect material for histopathological examination after a surgical consultation. Currently, based on the overall clinical picture, the progression of chronic lymphocytic leukaemia has been ruled out. Lymphoproliferation of NK cells with bone marrow involvement was diagnosed. Treatment of basic diseases was continued, as well as antiviral and antitumor treatment (ibrutinib, rituximab, Dexaven). Unfortunately, despite the treatment, the patient died due to a critical general condition.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 62-year-old man with a long-standing history of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) presented with recurrent infections, significant weight loss, weakness, low-grade fever, and abdominal pain.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Diagnosed with Rai stage II CLL in 2006 and initially treated with chlorambucil until 2010, the patient subsequently received FC (fludarabine + cyclophosphamide) in 2010 and subcutaneous immunoglobulin replacement starting March 2013 for hypogammaglobulinemia. In 2015, he relapsed with weakness, night sweats, peripheral lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, and WBC 68.5 K/uL, receiving BR (bendamustine + rituximab) and later CHOP in 2016, followed in late 2017 (when WBC rose to 131 K/uL) by rituximab plus ibrutinib and prophylactic lamivudine (for anti-HBc positivity). His course included pulmonary Candida tropicalis on 2017 bronchoscopy (treated with fluconazole) and colonic EBV-positive mucocutaneous ulcer with IBD-like lesions on colonoscopy. In 2021, he was hospitalized in the Department of Clinical Immunology for profound hypogammaglobulinemia, recurrent infections, significant weight loss, weakness, low-grade fever, and abdominal pain.
subjective.past_medical_history: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (Rai stage II, diagnosed 2006) treated sequentially with chlorambucil, FC, subcutaneous immunoglobulins, BR, CHOP, and rituximab plus ibrutinib; secondary hypogammaglobulinemia; EBV-positive colonic mucocutaneous ulcer/IBD lesions; paroxysmal atrial fibrillation; type 2 diabetes mellitus; Helicobacter pylori-positive erosive gastritis; atherosclerosis; resolved pulmonary Candida tropicalis infection; anti-HBc total positive on lamivudine prophylaxis (HBV and HCV negative).
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for significant weight loss, weakness, sweating, low-grade fever, abdominal pain, and recurrent infections.

objective.physical_examination: Peripheral lymphadenopathy and hepatosplenomegaly noted during disease course; subsequent lymph nodes were too small/inaccessible for surgical excisional biopsy in 2021.
objective.routine_investigations: 2010 baseline: WBC 11.87 K/uL, LUC 0.6 K/uL, lymphocytes 5.36 K/uL (45.1% CD5+CD23+CD19+), LDH 280 IU/L, beta-2 microglobulin 1.88 mg/L, normal RBC and platelets; 2013 immunoglobulins: IgG 4.85 g/L, IgM 0.14 g/L, IgA 0.34 g/L; 2015 relapse WBC 68.5 K/uL (80% monoclonal B-cells); 2017 WBC 131 K/uL. 2018 abdominal ultrasound showed hepatomegaly and enlarged periportal/hepatic hilar lymph nodes (1.09 x 0.77 cm and 1.14 x 0.53 cm) and colonic inflammatory changes. 2021 labs: deep hypogammaglobulinemia (IgG 1.83%), HbA1c 10.9%, WBC 11.68 K/uL, lymphocytes 7.27 K/uL (62.2%), microcytic anemia (RBC 5.06 M/uL, HGB 10.7 g/dL, HCT 35.8%, MCV 70.8 fL), transferrin 1.5 g/L (normal 2.0-3.6), serum iron 7.4 ug/mL (normal 50-212), fecal calprotectin 473.1 ug/g (normal <120), and CRP 44.0 mg/L.
objective.advanced_workup: 2017 chest CT showed right middle/lower lobe atelectatic-inflammatory changes; bronchoscopy with mediastinal lymph node biopsy confirmed CLL infiltration and BAL grew Candida tropicalis. Colonoscopy with biopsy demonstrated an EBV-positive mucocutaneous ulcer with IBD-like lesions. 2021 viral PCRs detected active CMV viremia (CMV-DNA 6.02 x 10^2 copies/mL) and EBV viremia (EBV-DNA 3.12 x 10^4 copies/mL, decreasing to 2.82 x 10^3 copies/mL after 2 doses of rituximab). 2021 peripheral blood flow cytometry excluded CLL cells and revealed 48.2% NK cells (CD2+ CD7+ CD3- CD16+ CD56+ CD8+/- CD4- Cyt3+/- CD38+ CD43+ CD5- CD19- CD30- CD34- TdT-); bone marrow trephine biopsy and myelogram confirmed ~10.1% NK-cell infiltration and ~20% small lymphoid infiltration (1/3 CD8+ T-cells) with complete absence of CLL infiltration.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Diagnosed with NK-cell lymphoproliferative disorder with bone marrow involvement (with complete regression/exclusion of prior CLL) complicated by deep secondary hypogammaglobulinemia and active cytomegalovirus (CMV-DNA 6.02 x 10^2 copies/mL) and Epstein-Barr virus (EBV-DNA 3.12 x 10^4 copies/mL) co-reactivation. Treated with valaciclovir and weekly rituximab (reducing viral load to 2.82 x 10^3 copies/mL after 2 doses) alongside ongoing ibrutinib, rituximab, and dexamethasone (Dexaven); however, the patient died due to critical general clinical deterioration.
